title_en: China Haohua Chemical (Group) Corporation v. Zhongqi International Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over a loan contract
ruling_gist_en: In concluding a contract, the parties explicitly agreed on a competent court to resolve potential disputes. Subsequently, the creditor's rights arising from the contract were transferred multiple times. However, none of the new creditors re-agreed with the debtor or the guarantor on a competent court, nor did they exclude the original contract's agreement on the competent court. As long as the original agreement on jurisdiction does not violate legal provisions, it shall be deemed to remain valid.

full_text_en:
China Haohua Chemical (Group) Corporation v. China Enterprise International Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

When parties to a contract explicitly agree on a competent court to resolve potential disputes, and thereafter the creditor's rights formed under the contract are transferred several times, if none of the new creditors re-negotiate the competent court with the debtor or the guarantor, nor exclude the originally agreed competent court in the contract, then the original agreement on competent court shall be deemed to remain effective, provided that it does not violate legal provisions.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 186

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): China Haohua Chemical (Group) Corporation, domiciled at No. 19 Xiaoying Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wang Yinhai, General Manager of the Company.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Enterprise International Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floor 32, Duhui International, Jinggang City Mansion, No. A3 Shilipu, Chaowai, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Qin Yingkai, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The Appellant, China Haohua Chemical (Group) Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Haohua Chemical Group), filed an appeal with this Court against the civil ruling (2006) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 1021 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case of a dispute over a loan contract with China Enterprise International Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Enterprise International). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Presiding Judge Jia Wei, Acting Judges Sha Ling and Yuan Duoran, to review the case. Yuan Hongxia served as the clerk.

The Beijing High People's Court found upon review: Although Article 11 of the Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract (Yi Gong Yin Gao Bao Zi No. 01) signed in 2000 between Haohua Chemical Group and the Yiyang County Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch) stipulated that "disputes shall be resolved through litigation in the court of Party B's (i.e., ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch) domicile," given that ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch, as the creditor who signed the contract, had assigned the creditor's rights through an assignment of creditor's rights, and China Enterprise International was the ultimate assignee of the rights after another assignment, a new creditor-debtor relationship was formed between China Enterprise International and Haohua Chemical Group. The agreement on territorial jurisdiction in the Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract signed between Haohua Chemical Group and ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch is not binding on the parties to this new legal relationship. Since the creditor, China Enterprise International, and Haohua Chemical Group did not reach an agreement on the competent court for dispute resolution, when China Enterprise International filed this lawsuit in the court of Haohua Chemical Group's domicile, i.e., the Beijing High People's Court, that court has jurisdiction over this case in accordance with the law. Therefore, Haohua Chemical Group's objection to jurisdiction, requesting a ruling to transfer the case to the Henan High People's Court, lacks legal basis and is not supported by this court. In accordance with Articles 22(2), 24, 38, and 140(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled to reject Haohua Chemical Group's challenge to the jurisdiction of this case.

Dissatisfied with the above civil ruling of the Beijing High People's Court, Haohua Chemical Group appealed to this Court, arguing: Based on the content of the two assignment agreements already submitted by China Enterprise International, both assignments of creditor's rights amounted to a general assignment of rights and obligations under the original guarantee contract. All assignees, including China Enterprise International, upon acquiring all the rights of the assignor under the original contract, should also assume and perform all the obligations of the assignor under the original contract, including the obligation to submit disputes to the territorial court that was lawfully and explicitly agreed upon between the assignor and the debtor. The original guarantee contract did not exclude the application of the dispute resolution clause. In the two written agreements for the assignment of creditor's rights, none of the assignees, including China Enterprise International, objected to the application of the original dispute resolution clause or expressed an intention not to be bound by it. Therefore, it should be presumed in accordance with the law that the assignees' true intention was to be bound by the dispute resolution clause in the original guarantee contract. The appellant requests that the court of second instance revoke the civil ruling of the Beijing High People's Court in accordance with the law and transfer the case to the Henan High People's Court for trial.

China Enterprise International responded: First, the assignment of creditor's rights creates a new legal relationship of creditor's rights and debts between China Enterprise International and Haohua Chemical Group, and the agreement on territorial jurisdiction in the original guarantee contract no longer binds the parties to the new legal relationship. The consequence of an assignment of creditor's rights is a change in the legal relationship and the extinction of the procedural rights of the original parties. The consequence of a change in the legal relationship and the extinction of the procedural rights of the original parties is that the agreement on procedural rights between the original parties no longer binds the parties to the new legal relationship. The original dispute resolution clause explicitly stipulated that the court of "Party B's" i.e., the creditor's domicile has jurisdiction, not that the courts of Henan Province have jurisdiction. This agreement is relative, not absolute. Since Henan Province is not the creditor's domicile, the courts of Henan Province do not have jurisdiction under that agreement. Second, the dispute resolution clause of the original guarantee contract, which is binding only on the original assignor of the contract and Haohua Chemical Group, is not binding on the parties in this case. The agreed place of jurisdiction only applies to the parties within that legal relationship. After China Enterprise International accepted the assignment of creditor's rights, the original creditor-debtor legal relationship was extinguished, ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch, the assignor under the original contract, lost its substantive rights, and its procedural rights also ceased to exist. Therefore, China Enterprise International did not assign the procedural rights that belonged only to the original creditor under the contract. The appellee requests that the court of second instance dismiss the appeal and affirm the original ruling.

Upon review, this Court finds: The creditor's rights claimed by China Enterprise International were assigned from the Zhengzhou Office of the Great Wall Asset Management Company, which had in turn assigned them from ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch. The original loan contracts and the maximum amount guarantee contract involved in this case all stipulated that any disputes shall be resolved through litigation in the court of ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch's domicile. The main creditor's rights involved in this case were transferred twice. The parties to the relevant assignment contracts for creditor's rights did not agree on a new competent court with the principal debtor and guarantor, nor did they exclude the jurisdiction clause in the loan contracts and the maximum amount guarantee contract. According to Article 3(2) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation No. 12 of 2001, "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases Involving Assets Formed from the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies," which states, "If the original creditor bank and the debtor have an agreement on competent court, and it does not violate legal provisions, such agreement shall continue to be effective," and according to Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Notice No. 62 of 2005, "Supplementary Notice on Issues Concerning the Acquisition and Disposal of Non-performing Bank Assets by Financial Asset Management Companies," which states, "After financial asset management companies accept non-performing loans and dispose of them through assignment of creditor's rights, they may apply the above provisions issued by this Court," it can be determined that the dispute resolution methods agreed upon in the original loan contracts and the maximum amount guarantee contract remain effective for the parties in this case. Furthermore, adjudication of the dispute arising from the guarantee contract between Haohua Chemical Group and China Enterprise International must be based on the relevant loan relationship. Since the domiciles of the original creditor, ICBC Yiyang County Sub-branch, and the principal debtor, Luoyang Zhonghao Chemical Industry Co., Ltd., are both in Henan Province, having the relevant court in Henan Province handle this case would facilitate the ascertainment of the facts. In accordance with the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on Issues Concerning the Acceptance of First-Instance Civil and Economic Dispute Cases by Higher People's Courts," the amount in dispute in this case meets the threshold for first-instance economic dispute cases accepted by the Henan High People's Court. Therefore, this case should be tried by the Henan High People's Court. In summary, Haohua Chemical Group's grounds for appeal are well-founded, and this Court accepts them. The original ruling, which rejected Haohua Chemical Group's challenge to the jurisdiction of this case, was improper and should be reversed. In accordance with Articles 25, 154, and 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court rules as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2006) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 1021 of the Beijing High People's Court is reversed.

2. This case is transferred to the Henan High People's Court for trial.

The acceptance fees for the first and second instances are 50 yuan each, totaling 100 yuan, to be borne by China Enterprise International Investment Co., Ltd.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Jia Wei
Acting Judge: Sha Ling
Acting Judge: Yuan Duoran

November 17, 2006

Clerk: Yuan Hongxia

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Jia Wei: Born in 1963, Master of Laws, appointed as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2006.
